item.description: Beth Macy is challenging Rep. Ben Cline in a bright-red Virginia district, hoping her own story and the stories she told about the region will win back rural and working-class White voters.

item.title: Trump lauded low prices at Freedom Fuel. A supplier says some gas wasn’t paid for.
item.description: A chain of gas stations that lowered prices last month in response to President Donald Trump’s call for cheaper fuel sparked a mystery over how it was able to sell at such a discount. A new lawsuit offers a possible answer: A fuel supplier alleges that it was not paid for gas that was ultimately delivered to stations in the Freedom Fuel Network.

item.description: Ranchers, taxi drivers and campsite owners on the Blackfeet reservation have endured two years of financial losses. They worry a new trade war will make things even worse.

item.title: Trump administration considering deal to give up part of Yosemite National Park to private developer
item.description: Under the potential deal, according to the National Parks Conservation Association and others, the federal government would exchange land that is part of Yosemite for property that directly borders the park held by Kingsbarn Realty Capital, a real estate investor.

item.description: The Trump administration is negotiating a long-term stake in a vast share of Venezuela’s oil fields, according to three people close to the discussions.

item.title: Trees are coming down by the dozen as Trump’s D.C. golf makeover nears
item.description: The president’s promised overhaul of the East Potomac course has not officially begun, but the tree removal has already been taking place for weeks.

item.title: FDA approves updated coronavirus vaccines for higher-risk Americans, including older adults and people with an underlying condition
item.description: The shots from vaccine manufacturers have an updated formulation aimed at better targeting the coronavirus variants circulating around the country. The companies said they expect the vaccines to be available in the coming days.

item.title: Putin sees U.S. as weakened by Iran war, intelligence reports say
item.description: The classified assessment of the Kremlin’s thinking preceded CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s secret trip to Moscow this week.

item.title: Stars and Stripes employees sue Pentagon over firings at military newspaper
item.description: The publication’s publisher, its editor in chief and a reporter allege that the government violated their First Amendment rights to free speech.

item.title: White House construction was a factor in safety incident with Trump’s Marine One helicopter, NTSB finds
item.description: The president’s helicopter took off from a temporary location due to White House construction earlier this month, leading to communication problems and a safety incident with Reagan National Airport, according to a preliminary report.

item.title: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America
item.description: The order requires that the U.S. Interior Department update geographic information systems to change the name of the lake, located between New York and Canada. The president said he’s making the change because “Canada has been ripping us off for a long time on trade, very sadly.”

item.title: $900 million from a canceled wind deal will benefit a Trump donor
item.description: The Trump administration’s latest deal to abandon offshore wind projects and boost investment in fossil fuels is set to deliver a windfall to a private equity fund run by one of President Donald Trump’s major donors.

item.title: What the disloyal leaks about Iran prove about Trump
item.description: Trump did what past leaders should have: Take an enemy at its word.

item.title: D.C. has never had a steakhouse as over-the-top — and fun — as this, food critic Elazar Sontag writes
item.description: At Ox & Olive, chef Ryan Ratino’s new Georgetown steakhouse, you’ll find some of the best steak in D.C. And a whole lot more beef.

item.title: Pirro’s special grand jury is investigating D.C. schools and city oversight of youth
item.description: The unusual investigation appears to have a broad scope. Prosecutors have contacted D.C. Public Schools personnel to question them about truancy and graduation rates.

item.title: ICE agent charged in shooting of immigrant is released from Texas jail amid Minnesota extradition fight
item.description: Christian Castro is accused of shooting and injuring a Venezuelan immigrant in Minneapolis, and then lying about the circumstances of the shooting.

item.title: Ratko Mladic, Bosnian Serb commander found guilty of genocide, dies at 84
item.description: He was serving a life sentence for his role in the Bosnian War, when he led forces that pounded Sarajevo and carried out the Srebrenica massacre, Europe’s biggest atrocity since World War II.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama dies at 97. The pop-culture fixture created art that evoked hallucinatory wonder.
item.description: The Japanese artist found global recognition late in life through her polka-dot paintings and mirrored, Instagram-friendly “infinity rooms,” with her hypnotic, unconventional works propelling her from near-obscurity to a place in the world’s most prominent museums.

item.title: U.S. weapons shortage from Iran war alarms allies confronting China
item.description: Concerns are growing in Asia and within the Pentagon that dwindling stockpiles will embolden China and North Korea.

item.title: Bill Gates was an AI optimist. Now he’s scared of what could go wrong.
item.description: In an essay, the Microsoft co-founder sounds the alarm about artificial intelligence’s risks to safety and security, jobs and children’s well-being.

item.title: FDA approves pancreatic cancer drug that in trials extended patients’ lives
item.description: Revolution Medicines’ drug, known as Rasonque or daraxonrasib, nearly doubled patients’ average survival times in treating one of the deadliest cancers, the agency said. The Food and Drug Administration had expanded access for daraxonrasib in May as it underwent review, stating that the drug met a critical need in treating pancreatic cancer.

item.title: Tim Curry, a British actor who found cult stardom in ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ dies at 80
item.description: Mr. Curry also appeared in the movies “Clue” and “Home Alone 2,” and he received Tony nominations for his stage work. His death was confirmed to the Associated Press by Marcia Hurwitz, his agent and manager, who did not cite a cause.

item.title: At least 75 dead, hundreds missing in flash floods on Nepal-China border
item.description: An avalanche caused the Bhotekoshi River to overflow, sending waves of water and mud that swept buildings and people away.
